$comment: Phase 12 (Scheduling & Timetable Intelligence) resolved against repository artefacts: architecture/phase-12-scheduling-intelligence.md (A..EU; ER domain neutrality for every organization, ES query model, ET memory and knowledge model, EU data model added this phase), frontend/src/lib/kernel/phase-contracts/phase-12-scheduling-intelligence.ts, registry row 12, the six scheduling-* modules and their six suites, and the /super-admin/scheduling-intelligence surface. Classified by scripts/audit-phase-acceptance.mjs. DECLARED areas are unfinished work reported rather than glossed: the engines are executable, tested and explained, while solver wiring, asynchronous runs, interop adapters, approval workflow, DST rules and learned solver selection have no artefact yet.

documentIntegrity.finding: The blueprint stated 16 of the 20 mandatory engineering sections: the query model, memory model, knowledge model and data model were absent. Sections ER, ES, ET and EU were authored in the document's own lettered style, and ER states the correction the rest of the document needed — that learner, instructor and class are one institution's vocabulary for a platform capability whose participants and resources are institutional data, so a hospital, company, warehouse or ministry configures the same engine in its own terms.

ownership.note: Phase 12 owns scheduling semantics: constraints and their priorities, availability interpretation, conflict detection and classification, conflict resolution strategy, optimization compilation, schedule generation, versioning, publication state, simulation, quality scoring, change management and explanation. Identity is Phase 02's, tenancy Phase 03's, canonical institutional reality Phase 04's, application runtime Phase 05's, workspaces Phase 06's, agent lifecycle Phase 07's, authorization Phase 08's, trust and provenance Phase 09's, delivery Phase 10's, academic requirements Phase 11's, financial effects Phase 13's, generic data infrastructure Phase 14's, hardware signals Phase 15's, digital twins Phase 16's, workflow automation Phase 17's and cross-platform analytics Phase 18's. Scheduling owns placement, never the records it schedules around.

areas.area: Conflicts are first-class, classified records
areas.requirement: Collisions are represented explicitly with a type, severity, involved entities, the constraint violated, a detection timestamp, a state and proposed resolutions, covering time, resource, participant, capacity, capability, policy, travel, accessibility, calendar, dependency, publication and concurrency.

areas.area: Participants and resources cannot be in two places at once
areas.requirement: Two overlapping activities sharing a participant or a resource are reported as blocking conflicts naming the participants and resources involved.

evidence.contains: detects a participant required by two overlapping activities

areas.area: Declared capacity is refused rather than assumed
areas.requirement: An assignment whose participant count exceeds a resource's declared capacity is a blocking conflict that states both numbers, and a shortfall of turnaround time between two uses is reported too.

evidence.contains: treats exceedance of declared capacity as blocking

areas.area: Blocked periods and closures cannot be scheduled through
areas.requirement: A holiday, maintenance window or emergency closure is represented as a blocked period; an activity inside one is a critical conflict, never a preference.

evidence.contains: treats a blocked period as policy, not preference

areas.area: Capability and accessibility requirements are constraints
areas.requirement: A resource that cannot supply a demanded capability is a blocking capability conflict, and a resource that does not meet a declared accessibility requirement is reported rather than silently accepted.

evidence.contains: detects a missing capability and a missing accessibility requirement

areas.area: Impossible transitions between sites are detected
areas.requirement: Where physical movement matters, the engine compares the available gap against the required travel time between resources and reports an impossible transition instead of assuming it is possible.

evidence.contains: detects impossible travel between two resources

areas.area: An infeasible request is reported as infeasible
areas.requirement: Blocking conflicts are separated from waivable ones, feasibility is stated, and guidance is returned; no fabricated valid plan is produced and a hard constraint is never waived silently.

evidence.contains: reports infeasibility instead of inventing a valid plan

areas.area: Feasibility is never traded for efficiency
areas.requirement: A plan is scored across independent dimensions, feasibility is binary and derived from blocking conflicts, and disruption and stability are declared unmeasured where no change exists to measure.

evidence.contains: marks a plan with a blocking conflict as infeasible

areas.area: A change is judged by the disruption it causes
areas.requirement: The number of changed assignments, affected participants and affected resources is measured against an explicit stability tolerance, and feasible candidates are ranked by disruption before quality.

evidence.contains: ranks feasible, least-disruptive candidates ahead of merely efficient ones

areas.area: Versions are comparable and changes are impact-assessed
areas.requirement: Two versions are compared by placement, resource, participant and conflict; a proposed change states affected activities, participants, resources and the least disruptive adjustment, escalating what it cannot resolve.

evidence.contains: calculates impact and demands a narrower change when scope is too wide

areas.area: Every placement can be explained
areas.requirement: A placement answers why it is here, why this resource was chosen, which constraints decided it, which preferences were sacrificed and why the alternatives were rejected.

evidence.contains: why here, why this resource, why not the alternatives

areas.area: Fairness is measured, not asserted
areas.requirement: Load balance across participants or resources is computed from committed load, so an unfair allocation is visible as a number rather than a claim.

areas.area: The capability belongs to the platform, not to one institution
areas.requirement: The engines schedule participants, resources and activities as institutional data; no kernel rule is stated in one organization's vocabulary, and the phase surface shows the same capability in the language of education, healthcare, logistics, warehousing, government and manufacturing.

evidence.contains: ER. Domain-Neutral Scheduling For Every Organization
names no runtime and no customer in its declarations

areas.area: The blueprint states all twenty mandatory engineering sections
areas.requirement: API, event, command, query, policy, security, tenancy, workflow, agent, memory, knowledge, observability, testing, audit, dependency, boundary, ownership, failure, data model and migration semantics are all stated; ER, ES, ET and EU were authored this phase for the four that were missing.

areas.area: A solver is attached behind the abstraction
areas.requirement: The same validator scores, ranks and explains any candidate plan, so a solver can be attached behind the abstraction; no external solver is wired, so no plan is currently produced by one.

areas.area: Optimization runs asynchronously and can be cancelled
areas.requirement: Long-running jobs need progress and controlled cancellation. The domain reports run state; the queue, progress and cancellation belong to the runtime and workflow phases.

areas.area: External calendars and systems import through adapters
areas.requirement: External calendar, HR and room-management systems require adapters with their schemas isolated. Import validation is specified but no adapter is wired.

areas.area: Publication approval is a workflow
areas.requirement: Phase 12 supplies the validation and the version a publication needs; the approval workflow itself belongs to the workflow phase and is not implemented here.

areas.area: Daylight-saving transitions are computed
areas.requirement: Every interval carries an explicit timezone and a missing timezone is refused, but a calendar conversion engine that resolves daylight-saving transitions is not implemented.

areas.area: Solver selection is learned from problem shape
areas.requirement: Learned heuristics, solver selection and quality learning are described by the blueprint and not implemented; any learning must remain subordinate to deterministic feasibility validation.
